fatal_errors: The material is incorrectly described as a single-phase solid solution; the target is an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy containing FCC and B2 phases.
The intervention lacks the critical aging temperatures and reverses the scientific emphasis: the target concerns embrittlement near 600°C and ductility recovery near 750°C.

The proposed mechanism of merely preventing detrimental-phase formation omits L12 ordering, increased antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, jagged FCC/B2 boundaries, dislocation pile-ups, and crack initiation at boundary tips.
No testable temperature boundary or non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile prediction is provided.
The cited evidence concerns different alloys and phenomena and does not support the claimed efficacy of the unspecified thermal treatment.
explanation: The hypothesis only matches the broad themes of thermal treatment, microstructural stability, and post-exposure toughness. It does not reconstruct the alloy, its duplex initial state, the 550–750°C brittle window, or the observed minimum in ductility around 600°C followed by recovery at 750°C. Its generic treated-versus-untreated comparison is nominally falsifiable, but unspecified treatment, exposure, loading, and microstructural criteria make it weakly discriminating. A target-aligned experiment would compare aging temperatures across and outside the brittle window while using TEM or TKD to test whether L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 boundary tips correlate with planar-slip pile-ups and crack initiation, while excluding impurity-driven intergranular embrittlement.
